title: Writing Through Church Hurt: Uncloseted Hearts Is Coming
excerpt: Writing Uncloseted Hearts has forced me to revisit church hurt, faith, identity, and what healing looks like when the wounds came from somewhere that was supposed to feel safe.
body:
Writing *Uncloseted Hearts* has been hard.

Part of that comes with writing the second book in a series. *Closeted
Hearts* introduced the world of Hearts Unveiled, and I want the next
story to feel like it belongs in that world while still standing firmly
on its own.

But there is another reason this book has been difficult to write.

This one gets personal.

## Writing about church hurt

*Uncloseted Hearts* follows Evan, a character introduced in *Closeted
Hearts*, as he deals with the aftermath of being hurt by a community
that was supposed to love him.

His story isn't my story. Evan is his own character, with his own
experiences, choices, relationships, and journey.

But I know church hurt.

I know what it feels like when a place that talks constantly about love
doesn't feel loving anymore. I know the confusion of trying to separate
God from the people who claim to speak for God. I know what it is like
to wonder whether there is still a place for you in a faith community
when being fully yourself seems to come with conditions.

And I know what it feels like to carry those wounds long after you've
left the place where you received them.

## When faith and identity collide

For a long time, being gay and being Christian felt like two identities
I was expected to keep fighting against each other.

There were prayers for change. There was shame. There were questions I
was afraid to ask out loud. There were moments in worship when I
wondered whether God saw me, heard me, or even wanted me there.

Those experiences don't disappear simply because you eventually begin
accepting yourself.

Sometimes your mind moves forward before your heart does.

Sometimes you leave the harmful theology but still hear its voice.

Sometimes you know intellectually that you don't believe something
anymore, but part of you is still afraid it might be true.

That tension became important to Evan's story.

## Healing isn't a straight line

I didn't want *Uncloseted Hearts* to tell a neat story where someone
gets hurt, learns an important lesson, and suddenly everything is fine.

That's not how healing has worked for me.

Healing has come in layers.

There are things I thought I had completely moved beyond that resurfaced
while writing this book. There have been memories I didn't expect to
revisit and emotions I didn't expect fictional scenes to bring back.

I've had moments when writing Evan made me angry.

I've had moments when it made me emotional.

But I've also had moments when writing him brought unexpected peace.

That's when I realized I wasn't only writing from the wounds anymore. I
was beginning to write from some of the scars.

## What happens after the hurt?

One of the questions underneath *Uncloseted Hearts* is what happens when
the institution that helped shape your understanding of God also becomes
responsible for some of your deepest spiritual wounds.

Do you walk away from faith completely?

Do you rebuild it?

Do you redefine what faith means?

Can you trust another church community?

Can you trust yourself?

And perhaps most importantly, can you stop seeing yourself through the
eyes of people who taught you that something fundamental about you
needed to change?

Evan has to wrestle with those questions.

I have wrestled with some of them too.

## More than a story about pain

I don't want *Uncloseted Hearts* to simply be a story about church hurt.

It's also about what comes afterward.

It's about reclaiming identity. It's about questioning beliefs you
inherited and deciding what you actually believe. It's about learning
that leaving a particular version of faith doesn't necessarily mean
abandoning God.

And because this is still a romance, it's also about letting someone
love you when experience has taught you to keep parts of yourself
protected.

There is pain in Evan's story, but there is also love.

There is anger, but there is hope.

There are questions without immediate answers.

There is healing that doesn't happen all at once.

## For anyone who has been hurt by church

If you've ever been hurt by a church, especially because of who you are,
I hope something in Evan's journey feels familiar.

I hope you see that questioning what you were taught doesn't
automatically make you faithless.

I hope you know that rebuilding your relationship with faith, whatever
that ultimately looks like for you, doesn't have to happen according to
someone else's timeline.

And I hope you know that the people who rejected you don't get the final
word on your worth.

*Uncloseted Hearts* is becoming one of the most personal things I've
written, even though Evan's story isn't mine.

Maybe that's what fiction can do.

It gives us enough distance to create something new while still allowing
us to tell the truth about feelings we've carried for years.

That's what I'm trying to do with Evan.

I'm writing about church hurt, but I'm also writing about what happens
when hurt doesn't get to be the end of the story.
